metadata.note: Modern-day BART network, as of the GTFS feed pulled from https://www.bart.gov/dev/schedules/google_transit.zip. Route geometry, frequency (headway_min, from real scheduled trip counts on a representative Wednesday), and avg_speed_kmh (from real scheduled trip duration) are all sourced directly from the agency's own GTFS feed, same methodology as data/amtrak.geojson. Each route is a single-year segment (2026) since GTFS has no historical depth. Historical segments (pre-2026) were added from BART's own published opening-date timeline and Wikipedia: the Sept 11 1972 Fremont-Oakland opening, the Sept 16 1974 Transbay Tube, and each later extension (Dublin/Pleasanton 1997, SFO/Millbrae 2003, Oakland Airport Connector 2014, Antioch/eBART 2018, Berryessa/North San Jose 2020). Each route appears twice in the GTFS feed, once per direction, and both directions carry the same history. Unlike the GTFS-sourced 2026 segment, the older headway_min values are estimates, not real timetables.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.line: BART: Antioch to SF Int'l Airport SFO/Millbrae

segments.note: The Concord line opened May 21 1973 from Concord to 12th St, Oakland. BART began revenue service Sept 11 1972 between Fremont and Oakland - 28 miles and 12 stations, the first all-new US heavy-rail system in over half a century, and formally dedicated at Lake Merritt Oct 11 1972. estimated era boundary/frequency based on researched milestone; no historical timetable found.
